_comment: 「KhmerSabaiの 朝礼」ページ（content/articles/asakai_team.json）の 絵の うち、文字を 焼く 11枚。noText は hourensou_zukai／asakai_zukai と 同じ 文を 逐語で 使う。文字を 焼かない 16枚は asakai_team.json。
style: Warm modern anime illustration, like a friendly Japanese educational manga — clean confident black linework, flat cel shading with gentle light, bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette of sky blue, cream and coral, rounded friendly shapes. A tidy contemporary Japanese software office with real desks, chairs, windows, plants, mugs and laptops. People are drawn as real human beings with natural proportions, warm friendly faces and exactly five fingers on each hand. Every picture is a REAL PLACE seen from a natural camera angle, and the subject FILLS THE WHOLE FRAME. This is a TEACHING picture, not a mood picture: what each person is doing must be readable from the picture alone. This one is a teaching diagram: few large elements, generous spacing, each label sitting on a soft cream panel with a rounded border, arranged so the eye reads it in one pass.
noText: Japanese lettering — read this part carefully. The picture contains ONLY the Japanese words listed in the scene above, and no other writing at all. Print each word LARGE and horizontally in a rounded gothic Japanese font, with generous space around it. Directly above every kanji, print its reading in small hiragana (furigana), centred over that kanji, clearly separated from it, at about 45% of the kanji height, so that the kanji and the furigana both stay sharp and easy to read at a glance. Words written only in hiragana or katakana take no furigana. Spell every character exactly as given. No other letters, numbers, logos or watermarks anywhere in the picture.
negative: Never: photo-realistic rendering, harsh shadows, extra or merged fingers, distorted hands, dark or scary mood, angry or crying faces, watermarks, real company logos or brand marks of any kind, national flags, country outlines, maps with borders, tiny cluttered text, paragraphs of text, 3D render, flat vector icon art, pictograms floating on an empty background, robots, mascots.

Card 1 holds a drawing of a ticket with a perforated edge and a shopping basket; its Japanese label is printed across the top of the card. Card 2 holds a drawing of a smartphone with one big rounded button and a finger pressing it; its Japanese label is printed across the top of the card. Card 3 holds a drawing of a large green circle with a thick white tick inside it; its Japanese label is printed across the top of the card. Few large elements, generous spacing, no people.

The screen shows a payment page: a heading panel across the top carrying its Japanese label, then three payment method rows each with a small square card drawing and a round radio mark; the FIRST row is clearly chosen — its radio mark is filled in sky blue, the row is framed with a thicker sky-blue border, and the row carries the words ABA Pay in plain rounded letters with no logo. At the bottom one big rounded sky-blue button. No people in the room. In the BOTTOM RIGHT CORNER of the picture there is a small round portrait inset with a thick cream border — inside it, the head and shoulders of the two new engineers — a young Cambodian woman in her early twenties with warm light-brown skin, a round friendly face and black hair tied back in a low ponytail, wearing a mint-green blouse and beige trousers, and a young Cambodian man in his early twenties with warm light-brown skin, short black hair with a neat side part, wearing a light blue short-sleeved shirt and dark grey chinos; both wear a lanyard with a blank white card. NEVER GIVE THESE TWO THE SAME FACE — she is clearly a woman and he is clearly a man, their two heads side by side inside the same round inset, facing the viewer with a calm friendly smile.
